description: What kody-os is and how apps get added, including the agent prompt and the setup guide pointer. No state, no actions.

files.index.html:
kody-os is a minimal shared OS shell. The home page shows your live widgets; the Apps page lists installed apps and opening one shows its live state, and every action runs through the same handler the agents use.

Adding apps

Copy this prompt into a Kody-connected agent and fill in the bracketed parts. The browser has no add control; the agent adds the app with MCP add_app — a registry write, no republish.

Add a new app to my hosted kody-os app on Kody. First open the published guide with Kody search entity package:kody-os#docs/adding-an-app.md, then follow that definition contract. Use the package's add_app through the Kody MCP execute wrapper. Validate before writing, verify with list_apps and get_app_state, and do not publish or change the package source. Do not add it to the homepage unless I ask. Ask me before writing if any detail is missing or ambiguous.

– App id: [slug]
– Name: [display name]
– What it does: [one sentence]

The new app appears on the Apps page immediately. Add it to the home dashboard from Apps → Edit → Add to home. Pins, hidden flags, homepage order, and recent use stay on this device.

Setting up a fresh fork or opening the OS for the first time? Follow the setup guide: open the published guide with Kody search entity package:kody-os#docs/setup.md and follow its sequence, ending with your first installed app.
